question: Can a receipt-guarded cedar reorder plan change the real optimizer path while preserving exact preprocessing output/RNG and a deterministic ResNet18 training trace, and can benefit/cost be measured without turning a contaminated calibration into final evidence?

arms.fail_closed_baseline: No receipts; the full region remains fixed and cedar optimizer execution is disabled.
arms.receipt_guarded_cedar: All three V2 pair receipts locally replay; cedar may select among six permutations using its fixed official profile.

semantic_endpoints: logit, gradient, and final model-state digests
performance_endpoints: preprocessing execution median/p95 and samples per second

hypotheses.h1_plan: Fail-closed exposes one candidate; complete V2 receipts expose six and cedar selects a different path.
hypotheses.h2_preprocess: For the fixed seed, both arms produce exact tensors, exception behavior, and RNG post-state.
hypotheses.h3_model: With identical labels, model initialization, optimizer, and thread count, both arms produce exact loss/logit/gradient/model-state traces.
hypotheses.h4_measurement: After one untimed warm-up, planning, preprocessing, paired/alternating training medians, cold/warm totals, and throughput are reported descriptively with no posthoc 5% gate.
hypotheses.h5_boundary: Synthetic probe images and P5K-P5M operators remain contaminated; the result is workload-harness calibration, not final benefit evidence.

pass_rule: All frozen/runtime/cedar checks pass, the plan changes, semantic/model endpoints are exact, and all performance fields are finite and positive; the performance direction itself is not a pass condition.
no_go_rule: Any output/RNG/model-trace mismatch revokes the current workload authorization; a speedup cannot compensate for semantic failure.
claim_boundary: Real cedar optimizer and ResNet18 execution on synthetic contaminated inputs. This calibrates workload measurement and semantic propagation only; it is not an independent dataset, final pair evaluation, or general training-speed claim.
